name: EMQX Edge
description: Lightweight MQTT broker for IoT Edge — EMQX Edge powers secure, scalable edge messaging with <5ms latency, 100K+ concurrent connections and 1M+ messages/sec.
featureList: Lightweight MQTT 5.0 & 3.1.1 brokering at the edge
High performance: <5ms latency, 100K+ concurrent connections, 1M+ messages/second
Ultra-low memory footprint (boot as low as 200KB; <10MB typical)
Cross-platform support for Linux, Windows, macOS, ARM, x86 and RISC-V; runs in Docker
SQL-based rule engine for local real-time data processing (coming soon)
Seamless, bi-directional cloud bridging (EMQX Cloud, AWS IoT, Azure IoT Hub)
Enterprise-grade security: TLS/SSL and multiple authentication methods including JWT
High-availability clustering and persistent store-and-forward buffering
REST API for configuration and monitoring; Prometheus metrics export
Integrates with OPC UA and Modbus via Neuron for IT/OT convergence

acceptedAnswer.text: EMQX Edge is a lightweight MQTT broker specifically designed for the industrial IoT edge. It runs on resource-constrained hardware (like industrial PCs and gateways) to manage local device-to-device communication, process data in real-time, and securely bridge data to the cloud.

mainEntity.name: How is EMQX Edge different from EMQX Neuron?

acceptedAnswer.text: They work together. EMQX Neuron is a connectivity gateway that collects data from various industrial protocols (like Modbus, OPC-UA) and converts it to MQTT. EMQX Edge is the MQTT broker that receives, processes, and routes that MQTT data. Neuron connects to the devices; Edge manages the data flow.

mainEntity.name: How is EMQX Edge different from EMQX Enterprise/Cloud?

acceptedAnswer.text: EMQX Edge is optimized for deployment on edge hardware with limited resources. EMQX Enterprise and Cloud are large-scale, clusterable platforms designed for high-availability, massive-scale deployments in data centers or the cloud. Edge bridges data to Enterprise or Cloud.

Yes. EMQX Edge operates autonomously to manage all local data communication. If the connection to the cloud is lost, it will buffer data (based on configuration) and automatically sync it once the connection is restored, ensuring no data loss.

EMQX Edge is free for use cases with up to 10 concurrent connections. For applications requiring more connections or commercial support, we offer commercial licenses (see: https://docs.emqx.com/en/emqx-edge/latest/license-policy.html).
